thesis: NVIDIA designs and sells accelerated computing platforms for artificial intelligence, data centers, gaming, professional visualization, and automotive. **[Fact]** Customers are hyperscale cloud providers, enterprises, PC gamers, creative professionals, and automakers. **[Fact]** FY2026 revenue was **$215.9 billion** (+65% versus last year); operating profit **$130.4 billion**; net income **$120.1 billion**. **[Fact]** The company reports four market platforms: Data Center (**$193.7 billion**, 90% of revenue), Gaming (**$16.0 billion**), Professional Visualization (**$3.2 billion**), and Automotive (**$2.3 billion**). **[Fact]** Cash to shareholders comes from operating cash flow after modest capital spending on labs and tooling, not from a lending or asset-management model.
why_market_wrong: There is **no clear dated mispricing signal** (HK predictive attribute: **none**). **[Inference]** The market prices NVIDIA as the default AI compute supplier with a widening software moat (CUDA), not as a cyclical semiconductor at trough earnings. **[Inference]** The debate is whether **growth deceleration from FY2026's peak** is already in the multiple at **~$140**, or whether networking attach, sovereign AI demand, and robotics platforms extend the growth runway beyond what a single blended growth rate captures.
